name: RetinAI
tagline: Web app that classifies eye diseases from fundus images plus patient age and sex.
description:
RetinAI is a web app that helps screen for eye disease. A user uploads a left and a right fundus image, enters the patient's age and sex, and gets a percentage score for eight categories: normal, diabetes, glaucoma, cataract, age-related macular degeneration, hypertension, pathological myopia and other. A built-in chart shows how often each category has been predicted so far. The interface is written in Bosnian.

I built the backend in Python with Flask and the models in Keras. The main classifier takes both eye images stacked into one 6-channel input, reduces it to 3 channels with a 1x1 convolution and passes it through an EfficientNetB0 backbone. A small dense branch for age and sex is merged with the image features before an 8-way sigmoid output. My training script follows the ODIR-5K dataset layout. It uses Adam, checkpointing that lets training resume, early stopping and learning-rate reduction. A second, MobileNetV2-based binary model checks that each upload is actually a retina image, and the app rejects anything else before it predicts.

What I would highlight is that I covered the whole workflow, not just the model. The app preprocesses images with OpenCV, stores prediction counts in SQLite and serves them to a Chart.js dashboard. After every 10 valid predictions it starts a background retraining job and blocks new uploads until the job finishes.

name: Knjigoteka
tagline: Bookstore and library system with an ASP.NET Core API, Flutter desktop and mobile apps, and Stripe.
description:
Knjigoteka is an information system for bookstores and libraries that digitises ordering, buying, borrowing, reservations and reviews. It has three roles. Admins manage books, branches, employees and restock approvals in a Flutter desktop app. Employees run branch sales and loans in the same app. Customers browse, order, reserve and review books in a Flutter mobile app and pay for orders through Stripe.

I built the backend as a layered ASP.NET Core 8 Web API. It uses EF Core with SQL Server and migrations, and JWT bearer authentication with role-based authorization. It applies migrations and seeds data on startup. Docker Compose runs the API, SQL Server, RabbitMQ and a separate .NET worker service together. Order checkout runs in a serializable transaction that validates central stock before decrementing it.

Two parts I would highlight. A background job runs every five minutes and expires unclaimed reservations, returns the stock and adds a penalty to the user. When a book is restocked or returned, the API publishes a message to RabbitMQ. A consumer service then emails the customers who asked to be notified, using MailKit. I also used ML.NET matrix factorization on co-purchase data to recommend related books. This was a university project for the Software Development 2 course at FIT Mostar.

name: NjamBa
tagline: Restaurant platform to discover venues, reserve tables, order and pay online
description:
NjamBa is a full-stack restaurant platform with an Angular front end and an ASP.NET Core Web API on SQL Server. Guests browse restaurants city by city, reserve tables, order from the menu, pay and leave reviews. Owners, waiters and admins each have their own screens for running a venue. I built it in a team of 2, and the Stripe card payments, Firebase image uploads and email verification all connect to external services.

I mainly focused on restaurant discovery, reservations, menu management, most of the owner and admin workflow, reviews and online payments. For discovery, the API returns a paginated, sortable city listing that can be filtered by menu category, delivery, rating band and a price tier computed from the average menu price. For reservations, it offers only tables that fit the party size and sector, enforces the venue's working hours and minimum lead time, and blocks overlapping bookings. Guests can cancel up to an hour ahead. A background service closes no-show reservations and adds penalty points, and an account is disabled at three.

Reviews are limited to users with a completed order at that restaurant, one per restaurant, with an optional photo stored in Firebase Storage. Card payments use Stripe PaymentIntents with Stripe.js on the front end, alongside a cash option. Paid orders also award loyalty points that can be redeemed for a discount. Owners add, edit and delete menu items with images and categories, and manage staff, tables, sectors and loyalty rules. Admins manage users, roles, venues, cities and categories.

name: CareFall
tagline: Fall-detection device on an ESP8266 that pushes alerts to a Firebase-backed web app.
description:
CareFall is an IoT project for fall detection. I built the firmware for an ESP8266 board with an MPU6050 motion sensor, plus an installable web app for managing devices and receiving alerts. When the device detects a fall, it switches on an LED and a buzzer. The wearer can silence it with a physical button.

On the hardware side, I wrote the Arduino C++ firmware. It reads the MPU6050 on all three axes, turns the readings into a single score and compares it to a threshold that is easy to change. It connects over WiFi to a Firebase Realtime Database. It reads a per-device notification delay from the database and, once that delay has passed without the alarm being cleared, writes a fall flag back. Pressing the button clears the alarm locally and resets the flag in the database.

The front end is a progressive web app in plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript, using the Firebase JavaScript SDK. It has a manifest and a service worker so it can be installed and show system notifications. The app lists registered devices with a status indicator. I added pages to register a device by its code and name, rename it, set the notification delay from 0 to 60 seconds, switch it active or inactive, and remove it. The pages poll the database and raise a notification when a fall is flagged on an active device. What I would highlight is that it connects embedded hardware, a cloud database and an installable app into one working loop.

name: Echelon
tagline: A 3D first-person Unity platformer featuring swinging, teleportation, and time-rewind abilities.
description:
Echelon is a 3D first-person game I built in Unity. The project has a tutorial level, five numbered levels, a main menu, a level-select screen and an options menu. Levels are about movement: the player can jump, dash in the air, slide on slopes, and use pickups that switch the right-mouse-button ability between a grappling-style swing, a throw-and-teleport projectile, and a rewind of the last few seconds of movement.

I wrote the gameplay in C# on a Rigidbody-based controller. A movement state machine (walking, air, dashing, grappling, swinging, rewinding and others) blends speed changes smoothly and keeps momentum after a dash. The swing ability uses a SpringJoint with an aim-assist sphere cast and adjustable cable length. The time rewind records the player's position and camera rotations each frame, then replays them with Lerp and Slerp. The teleport ability records the path of a thrown projectile and moves the player along it. I also added moving platforms that follow waypoints, checkpoints with respawn, and enemies that fire projectiles.

The part I would highlight is the progress system. A persistence manager finds every object that implements a small save/load interface. It writes level and battery-collectible progress as JSON in the player's data folder, with an optional XOR-based obfuscation. Levels load asynchronously behind a loading bar, and unlocked levels are tracked with PlayerPrefs. The project uses Unity's Universal Render Pipeline, Shader Graph and post-processing, and it includes some third-party asset packs, such as sound effects, shaders and particle packs, for the visuals and audio.

name: Hotel Pupo
tagline: A Windows desktop app for hotel room browsing, reservations and staff management, built in C#.
description:
Hotel Pupo is a desktop application for running a small hotel. It has two entry points from the welcome screen: a staff login and a "continue as guest" mode. Staff sign in with credentials checked against an Employees table, then reach a menu for managing guests, employees, rooms and reservations. Each of those screens supports adding, updating, deleting, searching and refreshing records, and double-clicking a row in the grid loads it back into the form for editing.

Guests can look through the four room types without logging in: a standard double, a double with separate beds, a double with a lake view and a single with a lake view. Hovering over a room shows its amenities, and a button opens a picture gallery with next and previous controls. From there a guest can start a reservation. The form lists only the free rooms of that type, asks for name, phone number, party size and arrival and departure dates (chosen with calendar pickers), then saves the guest and the reservation and marks the room as occupied.

I built it in C# with Windows Forms on .NET Framework 3.5, with 16 forms in the project. Data is stored in a Microsoft Access database accessed through ADO.NET (OleDb and a typed DataSet with table adapters). What I would highlight is that it covers the whole workflow end to end, from browsing rooms to a booking that updates room availability, with a separate staff back office for the underlying data.
